newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Christians challenge Manila peace accord in court.
newsitem.headline: Christians challenge Manila peace accord in court.

text.p: Nine Christian Filipino politicians on Tuesday asked the Supreme Court to void Manila's peace deal with Moslem rebels, saying it would lead to Moslem minority rule in a southern Philippine region where Christians predominate.

The politicians, including eight members of the House of Representatives and a provincial governor, accused President Fidel Ramos of abusing his powers by agreeing to the deal over Christian opposition.

The Ramos administration signed a peace agreement with the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) last month, ending a 24-year Moslem separatist revolt in the southern Mindanao region that has killed more than 120,000 people.

As part of the deal, Ramos installed MNLF chairman Nur Misuari as governor of a limited semi-autonomous area comprising four Moslem provinces. He has also created an administrative council to supervise development in 14 provinces, including those ruled by Christian politicians.

The council is to serve as forerunner for a wider autonomous region to be set up after three years and to include other provinces, including those run by Christians, which may vote to join it in a plebiscite.
The country's five million Moslem minority regard Mindanao as their ancestral homeland although they are now outnumbered 3-to-1 in the area by Christians.

"This insidious attempt to impose the will of the Moslems upon the predominantly Christian cities and provinces of southern Mindanao is set in motion by...a mere executive fiat," the nine politicians said in their petition.
The Supreme Court has not said when it will act on the appeal.
Ramos has said he is ready to answer any legal challenge to the peace deal.
